stem: A fintech company keeps its order-processing Lambda functions in a VPC and needs those functions to reach both Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams without any traffic crossing the public internet. Which TWO endpoint choices satisfy this? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Route both services' traffic through a NAT gateway placed in a public subnet
Add a gateway endpoint for DynamoDB to the VPC's route tables
Add a gateway endpoint for Kinesis Data Streams to the VPC's route tables
Attach an endpoint policy directly to the Lambda functions' execution roles
Create an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) for Kinesis Data Streams in the VPC

rationale: A gateway endpoint works for DynamoDB, so adding one to the VPC's route tables keeps that traffic on the AWS network with no network interface involved. Kinesis Data Streams is not one of the two services gateway endpoints support, so it needs an interface endpoint (PrivateLink), which creates an elastic network interface with a private IP that the functions can reach over DNS. Routing both services through a NAT gateway sends the traffic out through an internet gateway to each service's public endpoint, which is exactly the public-internet path the requirement rules out. Gateway endpoints only support Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, so one cannot be created for Kinesis Data Streams. An endpoint policy is a resource policy attached to the VPC endpoint itself to limit which principals and actions may use it; it is not something attached to a Lambda function's execution role.
